tasks.short: Learn from retail forums and conferences, then identify useful changes and security concerns.

steps.what: Choose relevant forums, conference sessions and subscriptions.
Read forum threads, newsletters and conference materials.

loop.input: A bounded batch of permitted forum posts, newsletters and conference materials.
loop.output: A short brief with source links, dated claims, disagreements and open questions.
loop.check: Require a source excerpt for each factual claim; check dates and flag unsupported security advice.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair per batch of up to twenty items; failed checks leave source-only notes.
loop.why_not_simpler: Useful techniques and caveats are expressed in free text across different sources.

steps.what: Attend conference discussions and ask peers about practical experience.
Select a retail experiment and record its hypothesis, owner and success measure.
Forward credible security concerns with supporting sources to the security team.

tasks.design: Configured subscriptions collect permitted material from the {OTHER} forum and conference platforms and the {EMAIL} into the {DOCS}. A bounded loop drafts a cited brief, and the merchant uses it to prepare peer discussions and proposals in the {PROJECT}; a configured flow forwards merchant-approved security concerns through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant information is scattered and mixed with promotion or anecdote. Summaries often lose the evidence needed to judge practical relevance.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-linked summarisation can reduce initial reading time. Existing subscriptions and simple collection flows provide most of the infrastructure.
tasks.still_hard: Peer credibility, applicability and weak signals need judgement. Private forums and conference material may restrict collection or reuse.
tasks.human_edge: The merchant asks useful questions, interprets lived experience and decides which ideas deserve a controlled trial.

ambition.what: Quarterly retail experiment clinic

tasks.altitude: The week contains more focused reading and better prepared peer conversations. The merchant can propose and, within delegated limits, lead small experiments; security changes still require specialist approval.

reach.task: Prioritise and evaluate retail marketing experiments.
reach.learn: Hypothesis design, baseline measures and stopping criteria.

reach.task: Turn validated learning into a usable retail procedure.
reach.learn: Evidence-based instructions, audience needs and document versioning.

evidence.claim: Configured subscriptions and bounded summaries can reduce discovery and initial reading work.
A documented Deloitte report contained non-existent sources and led to a partial refund, supporting explicit citation checks.

assumptions: Participation includes substantive conference or peer discussions, so the weak mail-share prior is not adopted literally.
Only permitted source material is collected; private discussions are not recorded by default.
Briefs support learning and do not automatically change retail or security settings.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
Access work covers source permissions, GDPR handling of participant data and EU AI Act applicability for the summariser.
unknowns: Which forums, subscriptions and conferences the merchant actually uses.
Whether their terms permit collection and summarisation.
The actual balance of reading, written participation and live discussions.
Who can authorise experiments and receive security concerns.
research_questions: Which collection methods preserve dates, authorship and stable source references?
How accurately can brief validation catch unsupported claims and stale security advice?
new_work: Review briefs and read the underlying sources for consequential claims.
Maintain source permissions, relevance filters and collection limits.
Remove stale or low-value sources.
Track experiment outcomes and route security concerns without treating summaries as verified advice.
tasks.statement: Participate in online forums or conferences to stay abreast of online retailing trends, techniques, or security threats.

tasks.short: Prepare approved product media, upload it to sales channels and check the live listings.

steps.what: Find approved media and match files to products and channels.
Resize, encode and rename media using {OTHER} media processing software.
Upload media, set gallery order and save listing changes.
Preview the gallery and approve its product association and sequence.
Publish approved media and check the live listing.

tasks.design: An integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reads approved packages from {DOCS}, validates product identifiers and produces an upload manifest. Configured media presets create channel derivatives, and connectors stage them in the {ECOMMERCE} for gallery approval. A {WORKFLOW} publishes the approved version, checks media availability and sends failures through {CHAT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Approval records, file names and product identifiers were disconnected. Different channel requirements encouraged repeated screen work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing media presets handle conversion. AI-assisted coding makes channel adapters, manifests and retry controls cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Some channels lack useful interfaces. Crops, gallery meaning and inconsistent product identifiers still create exceptions.
tasks.human_edge: The merchant spots misleading image sequences and chooses which views best answer customer questions.
tasks.altitude: Upload sessions become short gallery reviews and exception handling. Nothing changes in commercial decision rights.

reach.task: Check product gallery behaviour on mobile and with assistive technology.
reach.learn: Learn responsive media, keyboard navigation and accessible gallery descriptions.

evidence.claim: File conversion, identifier matching and media upload are predominantly deterministic operations.
Channel variation and visual gallery approval can limit fully unattended publication.

assumptions: Media creation and master approval are covered by the preceding task.
Channel-native bulk upload is configured first where it satisfies the requirements.
Human approval applies to the staged gallery; the publishing job cannot change its content or sequence.
Build ranges cover one storefront and one additional sales channel.
EU GDPR and EU AI Act requirements are assessed where relevant. National consultation rules are checked if the rollout introduces employee monitoring.
unknowns: Which channels support staging, bulk media upload and publication interfaces.
Whether product identifiers are reliable across channels.
How approval and rollback work in the current {ECOMMERCE}.
Which access permissions and national consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Can each channel preserve gallery order and avoid duplicate uploads after retries?
Which transformations need visual review rather than file-level validation?
new_work: Review staged galleries.
Resolve identifier mismatches and failed uploads.
Maintain channel format rules and connector credentials.
Monitor publication checks and remove duplicate derivatives.
tasks.statement: Upload digital media, such as photos, video, or scanned images to online storefront, auction sites, or other shopping Web sites.

tasks.short: Replenish merchandise using stock, demand, supplier constraints and available cash.

steps.what: Collect stock, sales, open orders, supplier lead times and purchase prices.
Calculate reorder quantities, stock cover and expected purchase cost.
Adjust quantities for promotions, seasonality, ageing stock and uncertain demand.
Confirm availability and negotiate delivery dates, pack sizes or substitutions with suppliers.
Approve the purchase commitment against budget and purchasing limits.
Submit the approved purchase order to the supplier.
Record supplier acknowledgement and chase missing or changed delivery commitments.

tasks.design: Connect stock and sales from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ECOMMERCE} to configured replenishment rules in the {PROCUREMENT}, with budget checks from the {ERP}. The merchant adjusts commercial assumptions and negotiates exceptions; approval releases an immutable purchase order for deterministic submission, acknowledgement matching and delivery alerts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Replenishment functions often existed, but inconsistent item identifiers, stale lead times and spreadsheet adjustments prevented dependable use.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing planning rules can be configured and connected more cheaply with AI-assisted coding. This does not require a new forecasting breakthrough or an autonomous buyer.
tasks.still_hard: New-product demand, promotions, supplier reliability and cash constraints remain uncertain. Portal-only suppliers and unstructured acknowledgements add integration cost.
tasks.human_edge: Balance cash, availability and assortment risk, and negotiate when suppliers cannot meet the plan.

ambition.what: A weekly campaign stock-risk decision before promotion spend is committed.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from compiling reorder sheets to reviewing demand assumptions and supplier risks. The merchant could gain authority to recommend campaign timing changes and move replenishment within agreed category limits.

reach.task: Align promotion timing and spend with available stock.
reach.learn: Campaign demand assumptions, contribution margin and the cost of promoting constrained products.

evidence.claim: Reorder points, lead-time demand, pack-size rules and budget checks can use deterministic planning functions.
Structured acknowledgements can be matched automatically; changed commercial terms require exception handling.

assumptions: The baseline includes a spreadsheet joining operational and purchasing data.
The purchasing system supports basic replenishment rules; custom calculations are needed only for gaps.
Submission accepts only an approved order version; changes invalidate its approval.
Structured supplier acknowledgements are processed automatically; free-text exceptions remain human.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.
unknowns: Which replenishment features are licensed and configured?
How accurate are stock, lead times and supplier item mappings?
Which suppliers support structured orders and acknowledgements?
What purchasing limits, cash restrictions and approval roles apply?
What access or employee consultation is required under national rules?
research_questions: Can existing planning functions represent pack sizes, minimum orders and promotional demand?
Can duplicate purchase submissions be prevented across supplier interfaces?
How should reorder rules be evaluated against historical stockouts and excess stock?
new_work: Maintain supplier mappings, lead times and replenishment parameters.
Review unusually large recommendations and stale input data.
Resolve acknowledgement mismatches and changed delivery commitments.
Monitor stockout, excess-stock and cash outcomes.
Maintain access controls; assess GDPR and EU AI Act applicability if personal data or AI components are added.
tasks.statement: Order or purchase merchandise to maintain optimal inventory levels.

tasks.short: Keep shipping supplies available, record stock and arrange replenishment.

steps.what: Count shipping supplies and inspect their condition at packing stations.
Enter counts and damaged quantities into the supplies register.
Compare stock, recent usage and delivery times to calculate replenishment needs.
Adjust replenishment for upcoming demand and approve the purchase requisition.
Check delivered supplies, restock packing stations and report discrepancies.

tasks.design: Configure a mobile count form in the {OPS_SYSTEM} so counts update the supplies register directly. A deterministic job combines packing volumes, stock, open orders and lead times to draft requisitions in the {PROCUREMENT}; the warehouse lead approves them before purchasing proceeds. Physical inspection, receipt checks and restocking remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Consumption is often poorly recorded, packaging units differ, and physical counts arrive separately from purchasing records.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing count forms and purchasing approvals cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding makes the remaining unit conversions and data connections cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Unrecorded waste, partial packs, supplier substitutions and physically moving supplies remain difficult to automate cheaply.
tasks.human_edge: Notice damaged materials and packing problems, and anticipate demand changes absent from recorded usage.

ambition.what: Weekly packaging safety-stock adjustments before promotion launches

tasks.altitude: The merchant spends less time copying counts and calculating quantities. The warehouse lead can gain delegated authority to adjust safety stock within an agreed working-capital limit.

reach.task: Compare packaging material use and damage rates across order types.
reach.learn: Packaging suitability, material measurement and the evidence needed for environmental claims.

evidence.claim: Stock registers, reorder calculations and requisition routing can use deterministic software.
Physical counting, inspection and restocking still require people without additional handling equipment.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: Reference workflow for a mid-size online retailer with an internal packing operation.
The build covers supplies tracking and requisition preparation; downstream purchasing remains a connected workflow.
No worker performance monitoring is proposed. GDPR applies to personal data; consultation follows applicable national rules.
unknowns: Whether shipping supplies are recorded in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, a workbook or an external warehouse's records.
Actual count accuracy, packing units, waste and replenishment lead times.
Available interfaces and purchasing approval limits.
Required access approvals and any applicable employee consultation.
research_questions: Does the existing {OPS_SYSTEM} already support mobile supplies counts and reorder thresholds?
Can packing events estimate consumption accurately enough to reduce count frequency?
new_work: Investigate differences between estimated consumption and physical counts.
Maintain packing units, supplier lead times and reorder thresholds.
Monitor failed register updates and duplicate requisitions.
tasks.statement: Maintain inventory of shipping supplies, such as boxes, labels, tape, bubble wrap, loose packing materials, or tape guns.

tasks.short: Align online retail plans with physical or catalogue channels.

steps.what: Collect channel sales, stock, promotion and fulfilment data into a comparison workbook.
Reconcile product codes, reporting periods, returns and channel cost definitions.
Calculate margin, stock allocation and promotion scenarios using agreed assumptions.
Choose a channel proposal considering customer behaviour, brand positioning and commercial uncertainty.
Agree channel responsibilities, operational constraints and trade-offs with channel and operations managers.
Approve channel priorities, budget limits and the proposed commercial tests.
Record approved actions, owners and deadlines in the shared delivery plan.
Review channel results and flag deviations requiring a revised proposal.

tasks.design: An integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconciles {ECOMMERCE}, {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} data, with explicit mapping exceptions and a deterministic scenario generator. The online merchant develops the proposal and negotiates trade-offs; the marketing manager approves commercial commitments. Configured flows in the {PROJECT} create actions from the approved plan, while the {BI} tracks results.
tasks.previous_blocker: Channel definitions and product codes differ. Comparable margin figures require manual reconciliation, while channel priorities require agreement across teams.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports and interfaces support scheduled reconciliation and scenario calculations. AI-assisted coding can reduce implementation effort without changing the underlying commercial uncertainty.
tasks.still_hard: Allocating shared costs, estimating channel substitution and resolving competing incentives remain difficult. External retail partners may provide incomplete or delayed data.
tasks.human_edge: Understand channel politics, assess uncertain customer behaviour and negotiate a commercially credible compromise.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of a cross-channel stock allocation experiment.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling channel comparisons toward evaluating experiments and resolving trade-offs. With explicit delegation, the merchant could select experiments within approved stock and budget limits; wider budget authority stays with the marketing manager.

reach.task: Evaluate cross-channel budget allocation.
reach.learn: Contribution margin, incrementality and the limits of channel attribution.

reach.task: Design a test of channel substitution.
reach.learn: Comparison groups, seasonality and uncertainty in small samples.

evidence.claim: Structured channel reconciliation, scenario calculation and reporting can use deterministic integrations and dashboards.
Cross-channel strategy still requires human commercial judgement and coordination.
The proposed time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.

assumptions: The online business coordinates with a physical or catalogue channel, directly or through a retail partner.
Core sales and stock records already reside in systems; a workbook bridges channel reporting.
The target solution uses aggregated commercial data and does not introduce employee monitoring.
Build ranges cover one channel comparison workflow and an initial set of agreed scenarios.
Consent and access time includes access approval and any applicable consultation under national rules; formal proceedings may take longer.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply where relevant; this design does not require model-based customer or worker scoring.
unknowns: Which physical or catalogue channels exist and who controls them.
Whether channel interfaces, exports and historical cost data are accessible.
Who can approve product mappings, cost definitions and commercial commitments.
Whether shared customer identifiers or employee-level data enter current reports.
Which national consultation requirements and internal approval processes apply.
research_questions: Can existing reporting configuration produce a sufficiently consistent channel comparison before custom integration is built?
Which scenario assumptions most affect the decision, and how can they be tested?
Can aggregate channel data answer the commercial question without linking customer identities?
new_work: Review unmapped products, missing feeds and unexplained reconciliation differences.
Maintain cost definitions and scenario assumptions when commercial arrangements change.
Check whether experiments measure incremental value or merely move sales between channels.
Maintain connector access and investigate failed refreshes.
tasks.statement: Integrate online retailing strategy with physical or catalogue retailing operations.

tasks.short: Set product prices using costs, market conditions, stock, and commercial goals.

steps.what: Gather purchase costs, stock, sales, fees, and return costs.
Review comparable market prices and current promotions.
Calculate candidate prices, margins, and discount effects.
Choose prices and resolve margin or positioning exceptions.
Check and publish the selected prices to the shop.
Check sales and margin results after price changes.

tasks.design: A scheduled calculation on the {DATA_PLATFORM} joins costs, stock, fees, and market observations into explainable price scenarios. The merchant reviews exceptions and approves each publication batch in the {ECOMMERCE}; the {BI} tracks margin and stock effects.
tasks.previous_blocker: Costs and market comparisons are fragmented, and pricing logic often lives in personal workbooks. Automatic publication was difficult to trust without visible margins and change history.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic calculations, validation rules, and publication checks can be assembled quickly. Numeric pricing decisions do not require a language model.
tasks.still_hard: Comparable products may differ materially, demand response is uncertain, and returns or fees can arrive late.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing commercial positioning and deciding when a lower margin serves a clear assortment or stock objective.

ambition.what: Daily markdown decisions for slow-moving stock.

tasks.altitude: The merchant reviews price exceptions and measured outcomes instead of rebuilding margin calculations. Delegated markdown limits could let them act daily within an agreed margin and inventory budget.

reach.task: Design a price-response experiment.
reach.learn: Comparable cohorts, seasonal effects, and why a sales change alone does not establish causation.

reach.task: Coordinate promotions with margin and stock objectives.
reach.learn: Campaign economics, promotional calendars, and interactions between discounts and advertising.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-7 working days; add national consultation periods if applicable

evidence.claim: Cost consolidation, margin scenarios, price validation, and batch publication can use deterministic technology.
Pricing outcomes require commercial interpretation because demand, promotions, and stock availability interact.

assumptions: Time shares and effort reductions are planning estimates.
The OTHER slot represents a market-price monitoring service.
Market observations are obtained through permitted access and can be matched to comparable products.
The initial scope uses product-level prices rather than personalised customer prices.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply where relevant; national pricing and consultation rules also need local assessment.
unknowns: Availability and freshness of costs, fees, returns, and market observations.
Current publication controls and support for reversing price batches.
Actual pricing authority and discount approval thresholds.
Applicable promotional-price requirements and national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Can existing shop configuration express the required pricing and publication rules?
Which missing costs most often create misleading margins?
Which product groups have enough comparable demand for a useful markdown experiment?
new_work: Maintain cost mappings, margin floors, and comparison rules.
Review unmatched products and unusual price movements.
Approve publication batches and investigate failed updates.
Evaluate experiments and refresh assumptions about demand.
tasks.statement: Determine and set product prices.

tasks.short: Publish accurate merchant details and approved transaction terms across online and offline materials.

steps.what: Retrieve and verify approved merchant identity, contact and registration details.
Select current transaction policies for the market, goods and sales channel.
Assemble merchant details and selected policies into online and offline disclosure drafts.
Review changed disclosures and authorize the exact release version.
Publish approved disclosures to storefront pages and transaction templates.
Insert approved disclosures into printable transaction materials.
Check rendered disclosures and retain publication evidence.

tasks.design: Keep versioned merchant details, approved clauses and market rules in the {DOCS}, with deterministic templates assembling each disclosure release. A named legal adviser authorizes the exact version through the {WORKFLOW}; publication to the {ECOMMERCE} and generation of print materials then use only that approved content. Automated completeness and version checks retain publication evidence and flag rendering defects for review.
tasks.previous_blocker: Merchant details and policies are copied across templates, while approvals in the {EMAIL} are difficult to tie to the version actually published.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned content, template generation and existing publishing controls already provide the necessary components. Small integrations can connect approval records to exact release versions.
tasks.still_hard: Legal applicability varies by market, goods and channel. Approved wording can still become unreadable or misplaced in a transaction journey.
tasks.human_edge: Decide whether terms accurately describe the transaction and whether customers can understand material restrictions before buying.

ambition.what: A reusable disclosure readiness check for new sales channels

tasks.altitude: The merchant manages release readiness and exceptions instead of repeatedly copying terms. They can gain authority to schedule publication within a legal adviser's approved release scope; legal interpretation remains with the adviser.

reach.task: Structure approved policies into reusable, readable disclosure modules.
reach.learn: Content modelling, version control and how to preserve legal meaning across formats.

reach.task: Prepare market-specific disclosure versions from approved source text.
reach.learn: Controlled terminology, locale requirements and review of legally meaningful differences.

evidence.claim: Approved clauses and structured merchant details can be assembled through deterministic templates without generating new legal wording.
Version-linked approval and publication checks can reduce mismatches between approved and published disclosures.
The digest supplies no disclosure-publishing implementation case; effort and build ranges are estimates.

assumptions: The first build covers one storefront and a limited set of approved print templates.
Legal advisers supply validated clauses and applicability rules; automation stops when no approved rule matches.
The release approval covers the exact online and print content, destinations and publication scope; subsequent delivery adds no discretion.
EU consumer and data-protection requirements apply, alongside market-specific national rules. No model loop is proposed.
unknowns: Actual selling countries, customer types, goods and disclosure obligations.
Where authoritative merchant details and approved translations are maintained.
Who may authorize releases and which changes require renewed legal review.
Whether publishing interfaces support version checks, rollback and transaction-template updates.
Required access approvals and any applicable employee consultation.
research_questions: Can existing {ECOMMERCE} templates reference one approved disclosure source?
Which disclosures need transaction-specific values rather than static text?
Can publication checks verify visibility and completeness across mobile, checkout and print layouts?
new_work: Maintain the approved clause library and market applicability rules.
Review unfamiliar transaction types and changed legal requirements.
Resolve rendering defects and failed publications.
Retire outdated templates and retain evidence of released versions.
tasks.statement: Disclose merchant information and terms and policies of transactions in online or offline materials.

tasks.short: Send transaction and shipment confirmations and resolve failed or incorrect notifications.

steps.what: Receive validated transaction or shipment events.
Populate the appropriate confirmation template with order and tracking details.
Send the confirmation and record delivery status.
Compare completed orders and shipments with confirmation delivery records.
Confirm contact corrections or explain conflicting shipment information to customers.
Check corrected details and resend the affected confirmation.

tasks.design: Configure transaction and shipment templates in the {ECOMMERCE}, using validated events from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and existing mail delivery. Add deterministic checks for missing events, failed delivery and duplicate sends, routing exceptions to the {HELPDESK}; staff verify sensitive corrections before a corrected message is sent.
tasks.previous_blocker: Routine confirmations were commonly automated already. The remaining gap was reliable shipment events, delivery visibility and safe correction handling.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing notification settings handle template generation and sending. Small event checks and controlled replay can close gaps without generating free text.
tasks.still_hard: Mail acceptance does not prove that a customer read a message. Incorrect contact details and conflicting dispatch evidence still require human resolution.
tasks.human_edge: Reassure customers and establish the correct facts when a confirmation conflicts with their experience.
tasks.altitude: Customer service checks fewer routine delivery records and spends more time resolving confusing orders. Decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Improve transaction and shipment confirmation templates.
reach.learn: Use clear status language, accessible formatting and consistent distinctions between order acceptance and dispatch.

evidence.claim: Transaction and shipment confirmations commonly use existing event triggers and fixed templates.
Missing-event checks and controlled retries can be deterministic; routine confirmations do not require a model.

assumptions: Routine sending is already automated; incremental gains concern monitoring and correction work.
The illustrative baseline allocates most human effort to checking and exceptions.
Event acceptance, capture and shipment have distinct definitions agreed with operations.
Routine templates contain service information; promotional messages follow separate rules.
Contact corrections require verification before customer information is disclosed.
Access estimates include GDPR review and any consultation required under national rules.
unknowns: Current notification configuration and the actual amount of manual checking.
Availability and meaning of delivery, bounce and shipment events.
Existing duplicate suppression, retry behaviour and supported languages.
Who can verify contact changes and approve corrected messages.
research_questions: Which existing notification settings cover partial shipments and delayed dispatch?
Which delivery events reliably distinguish retryable failures from permanent failures?
new_work: Review missing events, permanent bounces and contradictory shipment statuses.
Maintain templates, translations and trigger definitions.
Check duplicate suppression and approve corrected-message replays.
tasks.statement: Deliver e-mail confirmation of completed transactions and shipment.

tasks.short: Maintain sales orders and generate, deliver and retain accurate customer invoices.

steps.what: Import accepted sales orders into the finance order register.
Check invoice addresses, tax treatment, discounts and order totals.
Resolve invoice exceptions and approve departures from standard tax or commercial rules.
Generate numbered invoices from validated sales orders.
Send invoices through the customer's agreed delivery channel.
Save invoice copies and link them to orders for later retrieval.

tasks.design: Connect accepted orders from the {ECOMMERCE} to the {ERP}, then configure validation, invoice numbering and delivery using approved rules. Retain the authoritative invoice and order link in the {ERP}, removing duplicate filing in the {DOCS}; finance approves exceptional tax or commercial corrections.
tasks.previous_blocker: Order and finance records used different mappings, while invoice templates and tax rules needed local configuration. Document generation itself was usually already available.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing invoicing features cover most of the flow. AI coding can reduce the effort of field mapping, validation and integration checks.
tasks.still_hard: Cross-border tax treatment, credit notes and historical numbering errors need finance expertise. Invoice format and retention requirements depend on applicable national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Decide the correct treatment of unusual transactions and resolve disputes about what was sold or billed.

ambition.what: Customer self-service invoice retrieval linked to authenticated order history.

tasks.altitude: The administrator spends the week resolving incomplete orders and improving invoice accuracy instead of copying and filing records. Financial approval rights stay with finance; self-service retrieval is a separate extension.

reach.task: Write customer guidance for invoice retrieval and correction requests.
reach.learn: Explain invoice fields, authentication and correction routes in plain language.

evidence.claim: Sales-order validation and invoice generation are largely structured operations supported by standard finance software.
An authoritative invoice archive can remove duplicate manual filing when retention and retrieval requirements are met.

assumptions: This task concerns customer sales orders and invoices; merchandise purchasing belongs to procure-to-pay.
The baseline has an import step and manual delivery or filing around existing invoice generation.
Standard invoices use finance-approved tax and numbering rules.
Removing duplicate filing requires an adequate authoritative archive in the ERP.
Existing automatic invoice generation provides no additional saving by itself.
Estimates cover the core flow; the customer self-service extension needs separate scoping.
unknowns: Existing order integration, invoice delivery and archive capabilities.
Countries served, tax registrations and applicable electronic invoice requirements.
Actual exception volumes and approval responsibilities.
Retention requirements, access lead times and applicable employee consultation.
research_questions: Which invoice validation and delivery requirements apply to the intended markets?
Can configured archive and retrieval features remove the separate document copy?
new_work: Maintain invoice mappings, templates and approved validation rules.
Review rejected orders, delivery failures and numbering anomalies.
Verify archive completeness and access permissions.
tasks.statement: Create, manage, or automate orders or invoices, using order management or invoicing software.

tasks.short: Maintain accurate customer accounts across sales and customer records.

steps.what: Review new registrations and account changes in the {ECOMMERCE}.
Compare exports from the {ECOMMERCE} and {CRM} in a {SPREADSHEET}.
Resolve uncertain matches and conflicting details in the {CRM}.
Apply account changes and approved merges in the {CRM}.
Check incomplete records and failed updates in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: Configure validation and account records in the {ECOMMERCE} and {CRM}, adding a deterministic integration only where native synchronisation falls short. Stable identifiers permit routine updates; uncertain identity matches enter an exception queue, and merges require recorded approval before execution.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate identifiers, unclear field ownership and fragile exports made synchronisation expensive to maintain.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing validation and import features cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building mapping, retry and reconciliation code.
tasks.still_hard: Shared addresses, guest purchases and conflicting contact details remain difficult. GDPR purpose, retention and access requirements constrain which records may be linked.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a real duplicate from different people sharing contact details, and decide when evidence is insufficient.

ambition.what: Customer account continuity across guest purchases and registered accounts, after identity verification.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from copying records to resolving identity exceptions and preventing recurring data faults. Merge and access rights remain limited to the approved mandate.

reach.task: Prepare eligible customer segments for campaigns.
reach.learn: Learn consent provenance, suppression rules and the difference between account identity and marketing eligibility.

evidence.claim: Customer account validation, controlled imports and exception queues can usually be implemented without a model.
The proposed step shares, residual effort and delivery ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: The reference company uses separate customer records in the {ECOMMERCE} and {CRM}; a single master system would remove the comparison step.
Account data is mainly structured, consistent with the supplied prior; ambiguous identity decisions remain human.
The write gate applies to merges and disputed corrections. Validated routine updates run under configured rules.
Delivery ranges are working-day estimates for one account flow and may overlap.
The access estimate includes privacy review and any employee consultation required by national rules if working practices change.
unknowns: Which system owns each account field and identifier.
Whether native synchronisation, reliable APIs and change logs are available.
Actual duplicate rates, guest-account volumes and exception handling time.
Approved retention rules, merge rights and permitted uses of customer data.
research_questions: Can native synchronisation replace the export comparison entirely?
Which matching rules pass a labelled sample without false merges?
Can failed updates be replayed without duplicating or overwriting newer changes?
new_work: Review uncertain matches and approve merges.
Maintain field ownership and validation rules.
Investigate synchronisation failures and audit account changes.
Test mappings when account schemas change.
tasks.statement: Create or maintain database of customer accounts.

tasks.short: Create, approve and distribute printed promotional materials.

steps.what: Define the audience, offer, format, distribution route and print quantity.
Collect approved product facts, prices, images, offer terms and brand assets.
Write headlines, product copy and calls to action for the selected format.

loop.input: Print brief, approved product facts, offer terms and brand writing rules.
loop.output: Promotional copy draft with references to supplied facts.
loop.check: Validate prices, dates, links and length against source fields; flag unsupported claims for human correction.
loop.stop: One draft and at most one repair pass; missing facts or failed checks return to the merchant.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed wording covers routine stationery, but campaign headlines and persuasive copy vary with audience and offer.

steps.what: Lay out artwork in desktop publishing software using brand assets and printer specifications.
Check the proof and approve claims, prices, terms and visual presentation.
Send approved artwork and confirm the supplier quote, quantity and delivery instructions.
Inspect delivered print samples and resolve quantity, colour or finishing defects.
Insert materials into parcels or place them at agreed promotional locations.

tasks.design: A deterministic generator assembles approved facts from the {ECOMMERCE} and assets from the {DOCS}, then produces artwork from controlled templates. A bounded model loop drafts variable campaign copy, while people approve the proof and print commitment through the {WORKFLOW} and {PROCUREMENT}. Distribution instructions feed the {OPS_SYSTEM}; people inspect and handle the physical materials.
tasks.previous_blocker: Facts, images and offer terms are scattered across records and files. Repeated layout work and supplier correspondence persist even when the creative format changes little.
tasks.enabler_now: Template rendering, print-file validation and approval flows are established capabilities. Bounded text drafting and faster custom coding make it cheaper to connect them for smaller print runs.
tasks.still_hard: Original creative direction, unusual formats, image rights and physical print quality need judgement. Printed errors cannot be corrected remotely after distribution.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a message that fits the audience, recognise misleading implications and judge whether physical materials communicate well.

ambition.what: Small-batch promotional packs for collection-point partners.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from repeated copy and layout production toward campaign briefs, proof decisions and distribution experiments. Approval rights remain unchanged unless the organisation explicitly delegates a print budget.

reach.task: Prepare reusable print templates.
reach.learn: Typography, bleed, colour handling, image resolution and printer specifications.

reach.task: Check promotional proofs against approved source facts.
reach.learn: Offer consistency, claim substantiation and systematic proof correction.

evidence.claim: Product-description drafting is available today; this supports the copy step, not print production or distribution.

loop.check: Validate field lengths, required facts and prohibited claims; link factual assertions to approved sources.
loop.stop: One draft and one constrained revision; missing evidence or unresolved checks go to the editor.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover repeated specifications, but varied products need natural language tailored to intent and tone.

steps.what: Edit for accuracy, distinctiveness, clarity and acceptable claims.
Enter reviewed copy into product pages and campaign fields; inspect previews.
Approve and publish storefront copy or release subject lines to the campaign owner.

tasks.design: A generator combines approved facts from the {ECOMMERCE} and {DOCS} with a human content brief, using templates for specifications and a bounded model loop for prose. Deterministic checks stage the results in the {ECOMMERCE}, {CMS} and {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}; the merchant reviews the preview before publication or campaign handoff.
tasks.previous_blocker: Templates handled specifications but not varied prose; source gathering and copying into publishing fields remained manual.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded text generation is available today, while AI-assisted coding makes source mapping, field validation and publishing adapters cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Source quality, distinctive positioning, localisation and regulated claims still need judgement. Search performance is uncertain; fluent copy does not establish factual accuracy.
tasks.human_edge: Choose the promise customers should remember and judge whether the copy is credible and worth reading.

ambition.what: Useful buying guides for first-time customers unfamiliar with the product category.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward briefs, editorial decisions and testing customer understanding. The merchant could gain authority to commission guide topics and choose content experiments within the publishing policy.

reach.task: Map product pages to search intent and assess content experiments.
reach.learn: Query grouping, page intent, internal linking and measurement limits.

reach.task: Turn product specifications into clear buying guidance.
reach.learn: Source traceability, terminology control and explaining limitations.

evidence.claim: Shopify Sidekick supports generating product descriptions.
Structured field checks and source-linked editorial review can surround generated copy.

assumptions: Approved product facts and claims are available; the generator does not invent missing attributes.
Native draft and publishing controls are configured before building custom replacements.
Campaign sending remains a separate action with its existing approval.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.
Only necessary product material enters the model; GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties are assessed for the actual deployment.
unknowns: Which locales, product categories and claim restrictions apply?
Who owns final publication approval?
Are product facts versioned and linked to individual items?
What access and consultation requirements apply under national rules?
research_questions: Which existing generation and draft-management features satisfy the required controls?
Can all target fields be staged and previewed without publication?
Which factual and formatting checks can run deterministically?
new_work: Review unsupported claims, weak phrasing and localisation errors.
Maintain approved terminology, source mappings and generation instructions.
Check preview rendering and accessibility of supplied content.
Measure customer response without treating search ranking as guaranteed.
tasks.statement: Prepare or organize online storefront marketing material, including product descriptions or subject lines, optimizing content to search engine criteria.

tasks.short: Source, assess, and buy merchandise for online resale.

steps.what: Copy sales, stock, and open orders into a replenishment workbook.
Search supplier listings and identify available merchandise.
Inspect samples or used merchandise for condition, quality, and suitability.
Compare quoted prices, freight, minimum quantities, and expected resale margins.
Negotiate quantity, price, delivery, and condition guarantees.
Approve the purchase against budget, assortment needs, and supplier risk.
Submit the approved order and record the supplier confirmation.

tasks.design: Replace the copied workbook with a purchasing view fed by the {ECOMMERCE}, {OPS_SYSTEM}, and {PROCUREMENT}. Deterministic comparisons calculate costs and margins, while the merchant inspects goods and negotiates; an integration submits only the purchase approved in the {PROCUREMENT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier listings, stock records, and buying calculations use inconsistent identifiers and formats. Commercial judgement also made the whole task appear unsuitable for automation.
tasks.enabler_now: Small data adapters and calculation tools can be built faster. Existing purchasing approvals can control order submission without automating merchandise judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Used-item condition, uncertain resale demand, supplier reliability, and portals without stable interfaces.
tasks.human_edge: Judging saleability, detecting poor quality, and trading price against reliability and assortment fit.

ambition.what: A limited resale pilot for inspected returned merchandise.

tasks.altitude: The merchant spends less time copying figures and more time assessing stock quality and supplier opportunities. A delegated pilot budget could give them authority to test a returned-goods assortment within agreed loss limits.

reach.task: Validate demand for a returned-goods assortment.
reach.learn: Demand sampling, willingness-to-pay research, and separating stated interest from purchases.

reach.task: Assess evidence supporting reuse claims for returned merchandise.
reach.learn: Traceability, claim substantiation, and the limits of available lifecycle evidence.

build_days.consent_and_access: 3-10 working days; add national consultation periods if applicable

evidence.claim: Pactum checks requisitions against policy inside Coupa; this supports purchasing checks, not merchandise selection.
Stock consolidation, cost comparisons, and approved order submission can use deterministic technology.

assumptions: Time shares represent a blended buying cycle; physical inspection is concentrated in samples and used merchandise.
Structured supplier feeds or agreed quote templates cover enough purchases to justify integration.
Purchase submission uses the approval recorded in the preceding step; it does not require a second approval.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply where relevant. National consultation requirements depend on the implementation.
unknowns: Share of new, used, imported, and auction purchases.
Supplier feed availability, permitted access, and product identifier quality.
Approval thresholds, buying budgets, and supplier onboarding requirements.
Whether a returned-goods pilot is commercially and operationally feasible.
Applicable employee consultation and access requirements.
research_questions: Which supplier comparisons can use existing purchasing configuration?
How often do condition assessments overturn an apparently attractive margin?
Can supplier confirmations be matched reliably without reading free text?
new_work: Maintain supplier feeds, identifiers, and cost rules.
Resolve unmatched listings and incomplete quotes.
Check that submitted orders match approved quantities and terms.
Review demand assumptions and pilot resale outcomes.
tasks.statement: Purchase new or used items from online or physical sources for resale via retail or auction Web site.

tasks.short: Write and publish product descriptions from supplier information and verified product facts.

steps.what: Gather supplier specifications, existing descriptions and brand guidance.
Check source claims against product records and resolve missing attributes.

loop.input: Supplier specifications and product records for one product.
loop.output: Proposed attributes with source references, conflicts and missing fields.
loop.check: Validate field types and units; compare identifiers; require review of unsupported or conflicting claims.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction attempt per product; unresolved fields return to the online merchant.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured fields use direct mapping. Mixed prose and inconsistent specification layouts need extraction.

steps.what: Draft product descriptions using verified facts and brand guidance.
Approve accuracy, tone and customer-facing claims.
Enter approved descriptions into product listings and publish.

tasks.design: An intake integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} assembles sources from {DOCS} and {ERP}; a bounded extraction loop proposes facts for review. Configure description drafting in the {ECOMMERCE} from approved facts and guidance, using templates for standard specification sections. A {WORKFLOW} approval releases the exact approved copy through the {ECOMMERCE}, with version checks and publication logs.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier facts arrived in inconsistent documents. Copy tools and product records were poorly connected, so merchants gathered and re-entered information.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing description generators can be configured. AI-assisted coding lowers the effort of building source intake, validation and publishing connections.
tasks.still_hard: Unsupported claims, ambiguous specifications, specialist terminology and market-specific wording still need attention.
tasks.human_edge: The merchant decides which benefits matter to customers and whether a claim fairly represents the product.

ambition.what: Second-language product pages for one additional EU market.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from drafting and copying toward checking claims and improving weak listings. Additional market launches still require commercial approval; publication rights stay within the existing delegation.

reach.task: Review a reusable product style guide and terminology list.
reach.learn: Learn editorial consistency, claim qualification and how to write useful review criteria.

reach.task: Validate terminology for the additional market.
reach.learn: Learn locale-specific phrasing, units and when literal translation misleads.

evidence.claim: An existing commerce assistant can draft product descriptions; this supports trying configuration first.
Source assembly, field validation and approved-copy publishing can use deterministic integrations.

assumptions: The company has product identifiers shared across sources and listings.
A configured drafting feature can accept approved facts; otherwise a bounded drafting loop is needed.
Publication uses only the approved version; changed facts or copy trigger renewed approval.
Build ranges cover one storefront and one initial language.
EU GDPR and EU AI Act requirements are assessed for the actual deployment. National rules govern any employee consultation.
unknowns: Which drafting, approval and publishing capabilities the current {ECOMMERCE} provides.
Whether supplier documents may be processed by the proposed model service.
Who approves specialist claims and additional languages.
Which employee consultation and access approvals apply.
research_questions: Can configured drafting preserve every approved attribute without adding unsupported benefits?
Which source layouts produce extraction errors on a representative product sample?
new_work: Review extracted conflicts and missing attributes.
Check generated claims and maintain terminology.
Maintain source mappings and channel requirements.
Handle failed publications and version conflicts.
tasks.statement: Compose descriptions of merchandise for posting to online storefront, auction sites, or other shopping Web sites.

tasks.short: Combine sales and expense records, reconcile differences and calculate trading totals.

steps.what: Export orders, discounts, cancellations and refunds from the {ECOMMERCE}.
Retrieve booked revenue, fees and expenses from the {ERP}.
Match exports and flag missing entries or inconsistent totals.
Calculate sales, revenue and expense totals using workbook formulas.
Ask the finance team to explain missing costs and accounting differences.
Review totals and explanations, then release the trading report.

tasks.design: Configure scheduled exports from the {ECOMMERCE} and {ERP}; a deterministic job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconciles identifiers, periods and control totals. Configure agreed calculations in the {BI}, with source dates and unresolved differences visible beside the figures. A small records app in the {WORKFLOW} routes exceptions to the finance team and records the merchant's report approval without posting ledger adjustments.
tasks.previous_blocker: The arithmetic was already supported by software. Different exports, accounting definitions and missing cost entries kept reconciliation in workbooks and email.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduled exports and existing reporting features provide the base. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building mappings, controls and exception handling.
tasks.still_hard: Revenue recognition, VAT treatment, currency conversion, late refunds and shared-cost allocation require finance judgement and agreed definitions.
tasks.human_edge: The merchant interprets trading changes and challenges whether the figures reflect the commercial reality.

ambition.what: A daily channel contribution review using agreed attributable costs.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from collecting exports and rebuilding totals toward reviewing trading changes and resolving material differences. More frequent information supports recommendations; pricing and spending rights remain under existing delegations.

reach.task: Use channel contribution evidence to recommend campaign budget changes.
reach.learn: Learn cost attribution, uncertainty and the difference between revenue growth and profitable growth.

reach.role: market research analysts and marketing specialists
reach.task: Investigate whether sales changes reflect demand, seasonality or promotions.
reach.learn: Learn comparison design and how to avoid treating correlation as campaign impact.

evidence.claim: Sales and expense calculations usually need deterministic mappings, formulas and reconciliation controls.
A governed dashboard can replace repeated workbook preparation while leaving accounting exceptions with people.

assumptions: The {ERP} remains the source for booked financial amounts.
Trading reports are management reports; ledger changes and statutory filings are outside this build.
Customer-level personal data is excluded where aggregate records suffice.
Daily contribution is provisional until costs are complete and agreed.
Build ranges cover one ledger and one storefront, with existing reporting infrastructure.
EU GDPR and EU AI Act requirements are assessed for the deployment. National rules govern consultation if monitoring of employees is introduced.
unknowns: Which exports, scheduled reports and interfaces are available.
Whether sales and ledger records share stable matching identifiers.
Which revenue, tax, currency and cost-allocation definitions the finance team approves.
Whether daily attributable cost data is complete enough for contribution reporting.
Which financial access permissions and national consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Can reconciliation handle refunds, partial settlements and period cutoffs without silent double counting?
What freshness and completeness indicators make provisional daily figures useful?
new_work: Maintain account mappings and metric definitions.
Resolve unmatched records with the finance team.
Monitor missing feeds, late costs and reconciliation failures.
Review material changes before releasing reports.
tasks.statement: Calculate revenue, sales, and expenses, using financial accounting or spreadsheet software.

role_batches.altitude: The team shifts from copying records and checking routine statuses toward fulfilment exceptions, unsettled cash and customer remedies. Physical warehouse work remains substantial, and financial authority changes only through explicit delegation.
reach: Help marketing managers time campaigns against stock and fulfilment capacity.
Help editors and technical writers improve transactional messages and invoice guidance.
skills_to_grow: Map order, payment, invoice and shipment identifiers across systems.
Design duplicate protection, reconciliation rules and exception queues.
Interpret settlement evidence and recognise cases requiring finance judgement.
Use operational capacity and customer impact to prioritise exceptions.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run a daily trading operations review that connects promotion plans, fulfilment capacity, settlement exceptions and customer problems, with clear authority for each corrective action.

role_batches.altitude: The online merchant spends more of the week on assortment quality, difficult customer cases, and commercial experiments. New decision rights require explicit delegation of markdown limits, pilot buying budgets, and help-content changes.
reach: Market research: test demand and pricing assumptions with comparable evidence.
Technical writing: turn repeated customer questions into useful product and delivery guidance.
Digital interface design: reduce missing information in checkout and quotation forms.
Sustainability: substantiate reuse claims for a returned-goods assortment.
skills_to_grow: Data quality, configuration, and exception monitoring.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run a returned-goods assortment pilot with an agreed buying budget, inspected stock, clear condition descriptions, and measured margin and complaint outcomes.

role_batches.altitude: The merchant spends more time on product truth, visual direction and trading decisions, with less copying, uploading and workbook preparation. Automation does not itself grant new budget, pricing or accounting authority.
reach: Work with editors and translators on credible product pages for an additional market.
Work with graphic designers and interface designers on demonstrations and useful product galleries.
Work with marketing managers on channel contribution and campaign recommendations.
skills_to_grow: Product claim verification and editorial review.
Photography direction, colour fidelity and accessible media.
Financial reconciliation, metric definitions and cost attribution.
Exception handling and practical evaluation of automated outputs.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run a repeatable merchandising improvement service that combines trustworthy localized pages, product fit demonstrations and daily channel contribution reviews, within delegated commercial limits.

role_batches.altitude: The online merchant spends more time on customer remedies, product positioning, replenishment risk and placement experiments. Additional decision rights should be explicit: remedy limits, category purchasing flexibility, editorial scope and experiment allocation.
reach: Work with market research analysts to turn cancellation patterns into changes to product information and delivery promises.
Work with marketing managers to connect campaign commitments to stock and cash constraints.
Work with search marketing strategists and interface designers to improve product discovery.
Work with technical writers to make product claims clear and traceable.
skills_to_grow: Data quality, workflow controls and access management
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run a weekly commercial review connecting customer friction, product information, stock risk and discovery experiments, with delegated limits for remedies, replenishment adjustments and storefront tests.

role_batches.altitude: The merchant's week shifts toward product tests, commercial trade-offs and customer conversations. Wider budget or assortment rights require an explicit mandate; automation alone grants none.
reach: Search marketing strategist: diagnose feed exclusions and assess placement economics.
Market research analyst: design credible product-demand tests.
Advertising and promotions manager: recommend spending changes using incremental contribution.
skills_to_grow: Customer identity, consent and data-quality controls.
Structured campaign briefs and specialist collaboration.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run a small merchandising experiment programme that connects customer feedback, market evidence, product availability and campaign economics, with delegated test limits and explicit approval for larger commitments.

role_batches.altitude: The online merchant shifts from copying records and assembling reports toward stock exceptions, commercial experiments and investment choices. Approval rights expand only through explicit delegation of stock limits, experiment budgets and resource envelopes.
reach: Search Marketing Strategists: connect query demand to landing-page investment.
Web and Digital Interface Designers: turn funnel evidence into accessible experiments.
Marketing Managers: connect campaign budgets to margin and stock constraints.
Technical Writers: maintain reusable, versioned disclosure content.
Sustainability Specialists: measure packaging use alongside product protection.
skills_to_grow: Source verification and bounded model review
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run a regular commercial review that combines search demand, conversion, stock availability and contribution margin to choose one funded improvement at a time, then compare its outcome with the original hypothesis.

reach: Web and digital interface designer: evaluate shopping journeys and accessible interactions.
Marketing manager: assess service economics and channel dependencies.
Technical writer: improve digital access and recovery instructions.
Public relations specialist: assess naming and reputation risks.
skills_to_grow: Storefront component configuration and release testing
Customer research and cautious interpretation of conversion data
Supplier cost modelling and source verification
Digital entitlement controls and exception handling

They gain faster recommendations and potentially delegated trial decisions; buying, publication and technical security rights depend on explicit limits.
reach: Search Marketing Strategist: improve auction discoverability using buyer query evidence.
Market Research Analyst: test demand and uncertainty before trial purchases.
Sustainability Specialist: examine provenance and supplier claims.

Marketing Manager: design and evaluate retail experiments.

reach: Marketing managers: prepare and evaluate cross-channel commercial experiments.
Market research analysts: measure incremental channel effects.
Graphic designers: maintain reusable print formats and assess proofs.
